title: Windows Data Deduplication Job Health
exclusions: Monitors the most recent Windows Server Data Deduplication Optimization, Garbage Collection, and Integrity Scrubbing outcomes and their age for explicitly inventoried dedup-enabled volumes. It does not infer a job outcome from an event ID alone: a Deduplication Operational completion event can carry a nonzero error code. It does not measure active-job progress, predict savings, prove file readability, repair corruption, validate backup/restore, monitor ReFS/NTFS generally, cover non-Windows deduplication products, or establish regulatory assurance. `SavingsRate` and `OptimizedFilesSavingsRate` have different Microsoft-defined denominators and are retained for context, not used as job-success flags. Missing volumes, duplicate snapshots, command failures, unparseable result values, clock error, and incomplete manifests are source-health findings rather than healthy results. The example 15-minute collection cadence, 48-hour Optimization age, 10-day Garbage Collection age, 10-day Scrubbing age, and one-hour notification throttle are deployment policy choices, not Microsoft or Splunk defaults. The detector is read-only and must not start, stop, reschedule, or tune a deduplication job.
evidence: After deployment, retain the version-controlled `TA_windows_dedup_health` collector and normalized schema; exact collector identity and approved server/volume inventory; effective PowerShell input, parsing, routing, and access configuration; every complete manifest and volume row used by a result; raw `Get-DedupStatus` output captured at the same time for a bounded validation sample; relevant Microsoft-Windows-Deduplication/Operational XML events; the `windows_dedup_job_health` saved-search definition, ACL, schedule, dispatch history, result rows, and alert-action revision; source-health results; dashboard revision; policy and exception history; incident disposition; and dated positive, negative, boundary, stale, incomplete, duplicate, recovery, and upgrade tests. Preserve host, volume identity, sample/snapshot identity, all three result codes/messages/times, age thresholds, savings context, and indexing time. This documentation-only review created no Windows role, job, event, collector, Splunk search job, dashboard, alert, test fixture, or production evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated index with fixed dispatch time 2026-07-28T12:20:00Z, emit one schema-1 complete manifest and one volume row for `host=dedup-lab-01`, `volume_guid=\\?\Volume{11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111}\`, and `sample_epoch=1785240900`. Set expected/actual distinct volume count to one, `history_ready=1`, Optimization result `0x8007000e` at epoch 1785240000, Garbage Collection and Scrubbing result `0x00000000`, and valid 48-hour/10-day/10-day age policies. Expect exactly one row with `failed_jobs=optimization`, no stale job, and the exact nonzero result/message. Repeat with all results zero but `last_scrubbing_epoch=1784280000`, more than 864000 seconds old, and expect one `stale_jobs=scrubbing` row.
controlTest.negativeScenario: With the same fixed clock, expect zero primary rows when one complete volume has all three result codes `0x00000000`, Optimization age at exactly 172800 seconds, Garbage Collection and Scrubbing age exactly 864000 seconds, and `history_ready=1`. Also expect zero primary rows for each isolated malformed case: absent or duplicate manifest, `snapshot_complete=0`, expected volume count not equal to row or distinct volume count, duplicate volume GUID, two snapshots tied for the latest host epoch, sample older than 20 minutes, future sample, missing result/time, `history_ready=0`, wrong source/type/schema, invalid thresholds, or a volume absent from the inventory. A separate source-health search must report every rejected case. An exception test may suppress delivery for one exact host/volume and finite interval only after the base row is retained.

dataSources: Primary source: a deployment-owned read-only PowerShell collector runs Microsoft `Get-DedupStatus` on each approved Windows Server every 15 minutes and emits one complete JSON manifest plus one row per deduplication volume to deployment-local `index=windows`, `source=windows_dedup_status`, `sourcetype=ms:windows:dedup:status`. Required normalized fields include host, stable volume GUID/path, sample and snapshot IDs, `LastOptimizationResult/Message/Time`, `LastGarbageCollectionResult/Message/Time`, `LastScrubbingResult/Message/Time`, `SavingsRate`, `OptimizedFilesSavingsRate`, and governed age limits. Optional corroboration comes from XML collection of `Microsoft-Windows-Deduplication/Operational`; its provider, EventID, version, payload names, error code, job type, volume, and EventRecordID must be preserved. The Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows can transport Windows event channels but does not create the custom status snapshot.
app: A version-controlled deployment app such as `TA_windows_dedup_health` supplies the PowerShell collector, complete-snapshot schema, inventory/source-health search, primary saved search, dashboard, fixtures, and bounded exception lookup. Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742) is optional for XML Deduplication Operational event collection and parsing context; it is not authority for the custom `Get-DedupStatus` rows.
spl:
index=windows source=windows_dedup_status sourcetype="ms:windows:dedup:status" schema_version=1 (record_type="manifest" OR record_type="volume") earliest=-45m
| eval schema_version=tonumber(schema_version), sample_epoch=tonumber(sample_epoch), snapshot_epoch=tonumber(snapshot_epoch), snapshot_complete=tonumber(snapshot_complete), expected_volume_count=tonumber(expected_volume_count), history_ready=tonumber(history_ready), optimization_max_age_seconds=tonumber(optimization_max_age_seconds), garbage_collection_max_age_seconds=tonumber(garbage_collection_max_age_seconds), scrubbing_max_age_seconds=tonumber(scrubbing_max_age_seconds), last_optimization_epoch=tonumber(last_optimization_epoch), last_garbage_collection_epoch=tonumber(last_garbage_collection_epoch), last_scrubbing_epoch=tonumber(last_scrubbing_epoch), savings_rate_pct=tonumber(savings_rate_pct), optimized_files_savings_rate_pct=tonumber(optimized_files_savings_rate_pct)
| eval optimization_result=lower(trim(optimization_result)), garbage_collection_result=lower(trim(garbage_collection_result)), scrubbing_result=lower(trim(scrubbing_result))
| where schema_version=1 AND in(record_type,"manifest","volume") AND len(host)>0 AND len(snapshot_id)>0 AND sample_epoch>0 AND sample_epoch=floor(sample_epoch) AND snapshot_epoch>0 AND snapshot_epoch=floor(snapshot_epoch) AND abs(snapshot_epoch-sample_epoch)<=300 AND sample_epoch<=now()+60
| eval valid_volume=if(record_type="volume" AND len(volume_guid)>0 AND len(volume_path)>0 AND history_ready=1 AND match(optimization_result,"^0x[0-9a-f]{8}$") AND match(garbage_collection_result,"^0x[0-9a-f]{8}$") AND match(scrubbing_result,"^0x[0-9a-f]{8}$") AND last_optimization_epoch>0 AND last_garbage_collection_epoch>0 AND last_scrubbing_epoch>0 AND optimization_max_age_seconds>0 AND garbage_collection_max_age_seconds>0 AND scrubbing_max_age_seconds>0,1,0), manifest_expected=if(record_type="manifest",expected_volume_count,null()), manifest_complete=if(record_type="manifest",snapshot_complete,null())
| eventstats count(eval(record_type="manifest")) AS manifest_events count(eval(record_type="volume")) AS volume_events sum(valid_volume) AS valid_volume_events dc(eval(if(record_type="volume",lower(volume_guid),null()))) AS distinct_volumes values(manifest_expected) AS manifest_expected_values values(manifest_complete) AS manifest_complete_values by host snapshot_id sample_epoch snapshot_epoch
| where manifest_events=1 AND mvcount(manifest_expected_values)=1 AND mvcount(manifest_complete_values)=1
| eval expected_volume_count=tonumber(mvindex(manifest_expected_values,0)), snapshot_complete=tonumber(mvindex(manifest_complete_values,0))
| where snapshot_complete=1 AND expected_volume_count>0 AND expected_volume_count=floor(expected_volume_count) AND volume_events=expected_volume_count AND valid_volume_events=expected_volume_count AND distinct_volumes=expected_volume_count
| eventstats max(sample_epoch) AS latest_sample_epoch dc(eval(if(sample_epoch=latest_sample_epoch,snapshot_id,null()))) AS latest_snapshot_count by host
| where sample_epoch=latest_sample_epoch AND latest_snapshot_count=1 AND now()-sample_epoch<=1200 AND record_type="volume"
| eval optimization_age_seconds=now()-last_optimization_epoch, garbage_collection_age_seconds=now()-last_garbage_collection_epoch, scrubbing_age_seconds=now()-last_scrubbing_epoch
| eval failed_jobs=mvappend(if(optimization_result!="0x00000000","optimization",null()),if(garbage_collection_result!="0x00000000","garbage_collection",null()),if(scrubbing_result!="0x00000000","scrubbing",null())), stale_jobs=mvappend(if(optimization_age_seconds>optimization_max_age_seconds,"optimization",null()),if(garbage_collection_age_seconds>garbage_collection_max_age_seconds,"garbage_collection",null()),if(scrubbing_age_seconds>scrubbing_max_age_seconds,"scrubbing",null()))
| where mvcount(failed_jobs)>0 OR mvcount(stale_jobs)>0
| eval failed_jobs=mvjoin(failed_jobs,","), stale_jobs=mvjoin(stale_jobs,","), use_case="UC-1.2.61"
| table host volume_guid volume_path policy_id failed_jobs stale_jobs optimization_result optimization_result_message last_optimization_epoch optimization_age_seconds optimization_max_age_seconds garbage_collection_result garbage_collection_result_message last_garbage_collection_epoch garbage_collection_age_seconds garbage_collection_max_age_seconds scrubbing_result scrubbing_result_message last_scrubbing_epoch scrubbing_age_seconds scrubbing_max_age_seconds savings_rate_pct optimized_files_savings_rate_pct sample_epoch snapshot_id snapshot_epoch _indextime use_case
| sort 0 host volume_guid
description: Reports one row per deduplication volume when the latest complete `Get-DedupStatus` snapshot contains a nonzero result for Optimization, Garbage Collection, or Integrity Scrubbing, or when the last successful-or-failed recorded run is older than its governed maximum age. Snapshot completeness, volume identity, field shape, freshness, and result semantics are validated before evaluation.
value: Failed or overdue deduplication maintenance can leave incoming data unoptimized, retain unreferenced chunks, or delay discovery and repair of integrity problems. A volume-level result with the exact job code, message, age, and savings context lets storage teams distinguish scheduling drift from resource, filter-driver, corruption, or collection faults before capacity or restore risk grows. This reduces capacity and maintenance risk by identifying the exact deduplication volume and nonzero result that needs attention.
implementation: Deploy a signed, read-only `TA_windows_dedup_health` collector to approved deduplication servers. Every 15 minutes, normalize `Get-DedupStatus` into one complete manifest plus one row per volume, preserving all three last-result/message/time triplets and distinct savings-rate fields. Save the SPL as `windows_dedup_job_health`, schedule it after measured collection latency, alert on any nonzero result or age beyond the per-volume policy, and operate missing/incomplete snapshot health separately. Use Operational-channel XML only to explain the result; never classify a completion EventID as success without its payload.
visualization: Dashboard `Windows — Data Deduplication Health`: show expected servers/volumes with missing, stale, incomplete, duplicate, malformed, or command-failed snapshots before job findings. Add counts of failed and overdue volumes by job type; a table matching the SPL output with exact result messages and ages; 30-day lines for `SavingsRate` and `OptimizedFilesSavingsRate` on separately labelled series; and job-age distributions against policy. Drill down to raw status snapshots, same-time `Get-DedupStatus | Format-List *`, current `Get-DedupJob`, Deduplication Operational XML, volume free space, memory pressure, role/service state, schedule, cluster ownership, and change tickets. Never display absent status as zero failures or green.
schema: Custom complete Windows DeduplicationStatus JSON snapshot with optional native Deduplication Operational XML
dataModelAcceleration: No CIM model represents the three `Get-DedupStatus` last-result/message/time triplets, complete dedup-enabled volume inventory, or the two Microsoft-defined savings-rate denominators. A generic Change or Application State event count is not equivalent and no `cimSpl` is claimed. A purpose-built summary may replace raw snapshots only after it preserves complete-manifest, volume, result, age-policy, message, sample, and source-health fields and passes parity tests.

knownFalsePositives:
A returned row represents a real nonzero recorded result or a real age-policy breach in an accepted snapshot. It can still be planned, transient, or governed incorrectly.

1. **Approved maintenance, reboot, cluster move, or storage outage** — Jobs can be cancelled or delayed while a node, volume, CSV owner, or storage path is unavailable. Match the exact server, volume GUID, job type, change ticket, maintenance interval, cluster owner, and expected catch-up time. Keep collection/source health active and require a later zero result plus an in-policy timestamp before closure.

2. **Resource-governor cancellation during an expected workload peak** — Backup, antivirus, indexing, VDI boot storms, or application demand can leave too little memory, CPU, I/O, or free space for a deduplication job. Correlate the exact HRESULT/message, Microsoft Operational payload, memory/free-space counters, job schedule, and workload ID. Repeated cancellation is actionable even if expected; reschedule or tune only under storage change control.

3. **Newly enabled or restored volume without complete job history** — A volume can legitimately lack one or more last-job times before each maintenance type has run. The collector must set `history_ready=0`, and source health—not this primary alert—tracks the initialization deadline. Never synthesize a zero result or current timestamp.

4. **Deliberately infrequent Garbage Collection or Integrity Scrubbing policy** — Archive, offline, or constrained volumes may have approved intervals longer than the example ten days. Version a per-volume policy using recovery/restore objectives and Microsoft guidance, then boundary-test it. Do not raise the global threshold to conceal one exception.

5. **Cluster ownership or passive-node query mismatch** — A CSV status query from the wrong node can fail or return incomplete context. Verify current coordinator/owner, role installation on every node, target volume identity, and collector routing. Correct query authority instead of suppressing the volume.

6. **Manual diagnostic or repair job** — Storage engineers may intentionally run, stop, or restart Optimization, Scrubbing, Garbage Collection, or Unoptimization during an incident. Correlate operator, exact command, case/ticket, start/end, expected result, and follow-up status. Preserve the alert as incident evidence.

7. **Result-code normalization defect after Windows/module upgrade** — A changed CIM type, localized display, signed-versus-unsigned conversion, or parser revision can create a nonzero-looking string. Compare raw `Get-DedupStatus | Format-List *`, CIM type, hex conversion, collector version, and Operational event payload. Treat malformed codes as source health; never map unknown text to success.

8. **Stale time caused by clock or time-zone conversion error** — Cmdlet DateTime conversion performed without UTC normalization can make a recent job look old. Compare Windows Time Service, raw DateTime kind, UTC epoch conversion, event UTC time, and `_indextime`. Repair conversion and retain rejected evidence rather than adding a broad age exception.

**Safe suppression:** use lookup windows_dedup_health_exceptions.csv only after base detection. Require exact `host,volume_guid,job_type,policy_id`, inclusive numeric `valid_from_epoch`, exclusive `valid_until_epoch`, owner, approver, ticket, and reason. Reject wildcards, host-only entries, open-ended windows, and exceptions for missing, incomplete, duplicate, malformed, or stale telemetry. Suppression affects notification, not result retention, source health, or dashboard state.
mitreAttack: N/A (operational Windows Data Deduplication maintenance health; no adversary behavior or intent is asserted)
detectionType: Latest complete per-volume job-result and age-policy evaluation
hardware: Windows Server systems with the Data Deduplication role and one or more deduplication volumes. For Failover Clustering or Cluster Shared Volumes, every node must be qualified and the collector must query the current authoritative owner/coordinator under an explicit volume identity contract. Client Windows, non-Windows deduplication appliances, cloud storage optimization, backup-product deduplication, and volumes without Data Deduplication metadata are outside scope.
reviewer: documentation-only editorial review against primary Microsoft Data Deduplication run/status/job/install/troubleshooting documentation and primary Splunk PowerShell, Windows Event Log, and Microsoft Windows add-on documentation; collector schema, permissions, result conversion, manifest logic, SPL, thresholds, fixtures, Operational payloads, cluster behavior, dashboard, alerting, scale, and response were specified but not executed or Windows storage/Splunk-SME signed

cost.search_load_notes: At 15-minute cadence, each server emits 96 manifests plus 96 compact rows per deduplication volume daily. The saved search scans 45 minutes and performs bounded manifest reconciliation and latest-snapshot evaluation; optional Operational events are searched separately.

scriptExample:
```powershell
# Illustrative normalization core. Production code must add inventory,
# complete-manifest emission, non-overlap, error records, signing, and tests.
$SampleEpoch = [DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.ToUnixTimeSeconds()
$SnapshotId = [guid]::NewGuid().ToString()
$Statuses = @(Get-DedupStatus -ErrorAction Stop)
foreach ($Status in $Statuses) {
  [ordered]@{
    schema_version = 1; record_type = 'volume'; sample_epoch = $SampleEpoch
    snapshot_epoch = $SampleEpoch; snapshot_id = $SnapshotId
    volume_guid = [string]$Status.Volume; volume_path = [string]$Status.Volume
    optimization_result = ('0x{0:x8}' -f ([uint32]$Status.LastOptimizationResult))
    optimization_result_message = [string]$Status.LastOptimizationResultMessage
    last_optimization_epoch = ([DateTimeOffset]$Status.LastOptimizationTime).ToUnixTimeSeconds()
    garbage_collection_result = ('0x{0:x8}' -f ([uint32]$Status.LastGarbageCollectionResult))
    garbage_collection_result_message = [string]$Status.LastGarbageCollectionResultMessage
    last_garbage_collection_epoch = ([DateTimeOffset]$Status.LastGarbageCollectionTime).ToUnixTimeSeconds()
    scrubbing_result = ('0x{0:x8}' -f ([uint32]$Status.LastScrubbingResult))
    scrubbing_result_message = [string]$Status.LastScrubbingResultMessage
    last_scrubbing_epoch = ([DateTimeOffset]$Status.LastScrubbingTime).ToUnixTimeSeconds()
  } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
}
```
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and authoritative health contract

Assign Windows storage, cluster, Splunk collection/content, telemetry-health, and incident owners. Inventory every server, stable volume GUID, mount path, file-system/workload type, cluster role, deduplication usage type, expected job schedule, service owner, and retirement time. Install Data Deduplication only through the approved Windows role workflow. On clusters, confirm the role on all nodes and designate how the collector follows the current volume owner. The collector identity needs the tested read rights required to run `Get-DedupStatus`; it needs no permission to enable a volume, start/stop a job, alter a schedule, change memory, repair corruption, or move cluster ownership.

Microsoft makes `Get-DedupStatus` the straightforward authority for the last Optimization, Garbage Collection, and Integrity Scrubbing outcomes. A result value of zero means success. Preserve each corresponding result message and time. `Get-DedupJob` covers only active or queued work and therefore cannot replace last-completion history. Operational events provide detail, but EventID alone is insufficient: a completion event such as 6153 can include a nonzero error code. Parse provider payload by the XML field names observed on every qualified Windows build.

Define a versioned per-volume policy. The catalogue example collects every 15 minutes, considers the snapshot stale after 20 minutes, and reports a last Optimization older than 48 hours or Garbage Collection/Scrubbing older than ten days. These are examples, not product defaults. Set them from approved schedules, workload churn, capacity headroom, integrity objective, maintenance windows, cluster behavior, and measured collection delay. Use strict `age > limit`; exactly the limit is in policy. A volume is `history_ready=1` only after every required triplet is present and semantically valid.

## Step 1 — Build one complete normalized status snapshot

Run `Get-DedupStatus` locally or through a qualified CIM session. Inspect the real object with `Get-Member` on each supported Windows release before coding. Normalize stable volume GUID separately from mutable drive letter/mount path. Convert every HRESULT to exactly eight lowercase hexadecimal digits prefixed by `0x`; test signed and unsigned values. Convert DateTime values explicitly to UTC epoch seconds and retain raw values in diagnostic output. Do not translate an exception, null, localized message, or missing property into zero.

Create one `snapshot_id`, integer `sample_epoch`, and actual `snapshot_epoch` per server run. Emit one `volume` row for every inventoried deduplication volume, then one manifest only after all expected calls and validations succeed. The manifest's positive `expected_volume_count` must equal row count and distinct normalized GUID count. Set `snapshot_complete=1` only when no volume is missing or duplicated. A command failure, passive-node mismatch, invalid result/time, inventory disagreement, partial stdout, or serialization failure emits a separate collector-health record and no complete manifest.

Include the three governed age limits and immutable `policy_id` in each row. Preserve `SavingsRate` and `OptimizedFilesSavingsRate` as separate percentage fields; Microsoft documents different denominators, so never substitute one for the other. They are trend context, not a success test. Do not invoke `Get-DedupMetadata` on every interval: Microsoft notes that it performs a file-system scan, can conflict with optimization, and can consume memory.

Package the signed script in `TA_windows_dedup_health`, prevent overlapping executions, use atomic configuration updates, and log code/policy versions. PowerShell collection for Splunk Cloud runs on customer-managed Windows infrastructure and forwards events to the service; it does not execute in the managed search tier.

## Step 2 — Configure Splunk transport, parsing, and source health

Use an app-owned scheduled PowerShell input or protected spool monitored after atomic close. A representative local stanza is:

```ini
[powershell://windows_dedup_status]
script = . "$SplunkHome\etc\apps\TA_windows_dedup_health\bin\collect-dedup-status.ps1"
schedule = */15 * * * *
source = windows_dedup_status
sourcetype = ms:windows:dedup:status
index = windows
disabled = 0
```

Validate exact handler syntax on the deployed Splunk release. Configure one JSON object per event, `SHOULD_LINEMERGE=false`, an appropriate line breaker, and `KV_MODE=json` on the parsing/search tiers. Set `_time` from snapshot time or prove it remains within five minutes. Verify effective input and props precedence with `btool --debug`, index/RBAC, script identity/signature, output queues, duplicate deployment assignment, line truncation, and UTC conversion. Never edit an add-on's `default` directory.

Operate source health before job alerting. Compare complete manifests against the temporal inventory and report missing/retired/unknown volume; absent/multiple manifest; incomplete flag; expected/event/distinct mismatch; duplicate GUID; competing snapshot IDs at one latest epoch; stale/future sample; collection duration above policy; invalid result format; null/message/time; age limit <=0; unsupported schema; collector error; cluster owner mismatch; and clock/indexing delay. Missing status is unknown. It must never become zero error or current time.

Optionally collect **Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > Deduplication > Operational** as XML with a governed `[WinEventLog://Microsoft-Windows-Deduplication/Operational]` stanza. Verify the exact channel name in `wevtutil el`, enable XML rendering, preserve provider/EventID/version/EventRecordID/computer and named payload data, and test any `$XmlRegex` filter. Do not filter to a guessed static event list; Microsoft troubleshooting references multiple IDs and Windows releases can differ.

## Step 3 — Create and understand the primary search

Save the sidecar SPL as `windows_dedup_job_health`, schedule after the 15-minute sample plus measured p99 indexing allowance, and trigger when result count is greater than zero. Keep the bounded 45-minute base window. The first stages convert numeric controls, normalize result strings, and require valid integer sample/snapshot epochs. The per-volume predicate requires stable identity, all three exact result strings, three times, three positive age limits, and `history_ready=1`.

Manifest `eventstats` requires one manifest, one complete flag, positive integer expected count, and equality among expected, actual, valid, and distinct rows. The latest host epoch must map to exactly one snapshot and be no older than 20 minutes. These gates prevent partial collection from being evaluated. Rejected data belongs in source health.

For each accepted volume, the search computes age from dispatch time. Any code other than `0x00000000` adds that job to `failed_jobs`; age strictly greater than policy adds it to `stale_jobs`. A row can contain both. The exact code/message/time remains in output. The rule does not assert root cause from an HRESULT, infer that a stale job never ran, or claim that current savings decline is failure.

Use stateful incident logic keyed by exact host, volume GUID, job type, and policy. Throttle repeated delivery for one collection interval while retaining every result. Recover only after a complete newer snapshot has a zero result and age inside policy for the affected job. Missing data, a different mount letter, or exception expiry cannot close an incident.

No CIM/tstats equivalent is supplied. If scale requires a summary, write complete volume rows plus a manifest and prove raw/summary parity for failures, boundaries, missing rows, duplicates, latest selection, and retention before switching authority.

## Step 4 — Validate logic against PowerShell and Event Viewer

Use fixed-time isolated fixtures from `controlTest`. Assert the nonzero code case, stale-only case, and a row with both conditions. Boundary-test exactly 48 hours and ten days versus one second over. Test uppercase code normalization, signed-to-hex conversion, leap-day/time-zone handling, future/null/default DateTime, duplicate and incomplete snapshots, tied latest IDs, stale samples, invalid thresholds, Unicode volume paths/messages, and volume inventory add/remove. Every invalid case must produce source-health output and zero primary rows.

On two nonproduction servers, capture the collector row and immediately run:

```powershell
Get-DedupStatus | Format-List *
Get-DedupJob | Format-List *
Get-WinEvent -LogName 'Microsoft-Windows-Deduplication/Operational' -MaxEvents 50
```

Compare exact volume, result, message, time, savings fields, current jobs, and nearby XML events. In Server Manager compare **File and Storage Services > Volumes > Disks/Volumes** and the Data Deduplication configuration for the same volume. Allow only a documented bounded observation gap. Verify one cluster volume from its current owner and after a controlled ownership move in a lab.

Exercise synthetic JSON for failure logic; do not corrupt data or exhaust memory in production. If a lab test starts/stops a job, use a disposable dataset and approved procedure, then confirm the exact result and recovery snapshot. Measure script runtime, server impact, output bytes, indexing lag, Operational event rate, search runtime, and dashboard cardinality at fleet scale.

Keep `status=draft` until human storage, cluster, Windows, and Splunk owners accept exact versions, rights, schema, source health, policies, fixtures, alert delivery, dashboard, retention, suppression, recovery, and runbook. Documentation review alone is not runtime validation.

## Step 5 — Operationalize response and bounded exceptions

Build the dashboard in `visualization` with source trust first and access restricted to infrastructure operators. Alert text should state `Windows Data Deduplication job failed or exceeded age policy: <host>/<volume>`. Include job list, exact code/message/time and age, threshold, snapshot/sample times, current active job context, savings context with denominator labels, cluster owner, source health, owner, exception state, and runbook.

Responder sequence:
1. Verify the accepted complete snapshot, exact stable volume identity, current owner, policy, time conversion, and raw `Get-DedupStatus`.
2. Inspect `Get-DedupJob` and nearby Operational events; preserve named payload and error code rather than relying on rendered English text.
3. Confirm free space, memory, CPU/I/O, deduplication service/role/filter state, schedule, workload churn, backup/AV activity, Windows updates, storage/cluster events, and recent changes.
4. Follow Microsoft troubleshooting for the observed code. Escalate corruption, filter-driver, CSV ownership, or repeated resource failures to qualified storage support.
5. Choose a reviewed action: allow the next scheduled run, reschedule workload/job, correct role/cluster authority, restore resources, patch a supported issue, or perform Microsoft-supported repair. Capture before/after status and a complete recovery snapshot.

Never automatically run `Start-DedupJob`, `Stop-DedupJob`, `Update-DedupStatus`, change schedules/memory/registry, disable antivirus, move a cluster role, reboot, repair corruption, or delete data from this alert. Those actions can increase load, conflict with active work, or damage evidence. Require storage change control.

Apply only the exact finite exception contract in `knownFalsePositives`; suppress notification after detection, not collection, source health, result retention, or dashboard visibility. Review inventory, schedules, policy ages, collector rights/versions, cluster authority, exception expiry, and result parsing quarterly and after Windows, role, storage, cluster, PowerShell, forwarder, add-on, or Splunk changes.

## Step 6 — Troubleshoot without manufacturing success

- **No snapshot:** run the cmdlet under the collection identity, verify the role/module, script signature, input schedule, path, output queues, index route, and source-health error. No data is not healthy.
- **Volume absent:** compare approved inventory, `Get-DedupStatus`, mount/GUID mapping, dedup enablement, cluster owner, and retirement epoch. Never reduce expected count after partial collection.
- **Code looks negative or too long:** inspect the native type and normalize through `[uint32]` to eight hexadecimal digits. Do not compare localized decimal text.
- **Last time is year 1 or null:** job history is not ready or conversion failed. Set `history_ready=0` and investigate initialization; do not use collection time.
- **6153 appears but search says failure:** inspect its error-code payload. Completion does not mean successful completion.
- **Savings percentages disagree:** expected because Microsoft defines whole-volume and optimized-file denominators differently. Check field mapping and label both.
- **Operational channel is empty:** verify channel enabled/existing, exact stanza, XML mode, filter, checkpoint, permissions, and whether any relevant event occurred. The status snapshot remains primary.
- **CSV query fails on one node:** query the current owner/coordinator under the qualified cluster design and record ownership. Do not broaden administrator rights blindly.
- **Alert remains after a successful manual job:** wait for a complete newer snapshot, verify result/time for the same job/volume, policy, collector clock, and incident key.
- **CIM search is empty:** expected. There is no declared CIM equivalent for complete Data Deduplication status.
grandmaExplanation: We check whether the Windows jobs that save disk space, clean up old chunks, and inspect stored data have succeeded recently. If one fails or has not run on time, we show the exact volume and message so the storage team can investigate safely.
